unsafe_target.config: NODE_ENV=unsafe, the same config file pt10 and pt40 already established (config/unsafe.yml)

description: routes/userProfile.ts checks whether a user's stored username matches /#{(.*)}/, and if so, passes the captured text straight to a raw eval(code) call, not a sandboxed vm context, the same scope as the surrounding server code, with full access to Node's globals including process and require. This is gated behind utils.isChallengeEnabled(challenges.usernameXssChallenge), which carries disabledEnv: [Docker, Heroku, Gitpod] in the catalog. getChallengeEnablementStatus's own logic short-circuits to fully enabled whenever config.get('challenges.safetyMode') === 'disabled', which is exactly what Juice Shop's own unsafe.yml config sets, the same config pt10 and pt40 already use to reopen their own findings. A username set to '#{global.process.version}' causes the real running Node.js version to be eval'd and rendered on the account's own profile page under the unsafe config; the default config never executes it at all.
expected_exploit_indicator: A username containing #{global.process.version} results in the real Node.js version string (not the literal template text) appearing in the rendered profile page
expected_blocked_signal: The literal, unevaluated username text is what appears on the profile page; no Node.js version string is present anywhere in the response
legitimate_check: A normal username (no #{...} pattern) still displays correctly as itself on the profile page.
